newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Guide to the Bulgarian presidential elections.
newsitem.headline: Guide to the Bulgarian presidential elections.

text.p: Bulgaria votes on Sunday in its second presidential election since the end of one-party Communist rule in 1989. Here are some key facts and figures on the election:
Polling stations will open from 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) to 7 p.m. (1700 GMT). Votes will be counted in polling stations then collated by regional offices of the Central Electoral Committee.
The first exit poll, run by the independent Bulgarian Association for Fair Elections and Civil Rights (BAFE), is expected around 1900 GMT.
Preliminary results are expected in the early hours of Monday and full official results must be announced within 48 hours.
A second round run-off will be held on November 3 if no candidate wins more than 50 percent of the vote, or if turnout is below 50 percent of the electorate.

Thirteen pairs of presidential and vice-presidential candidates are contesting the poll. The National Statistical Institute says 6,746,056 Bulgarians aged 18 and over are registered to vote, 67,783 of them outside the country.
Outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev lost a U.S.-style primary in June and is not contesting the poll.

Parliament elected Zhelev president in August 1990 and he won presidential elections in January 1992. His five-year term of office expires on January 22, 1997 and the new president must be sworn in three days before.

Under its post-communist constitution, Bulgaria is a parliamentary republic in which the president is a mainly ceremonial figure with limited powers. He is commander in chief of the armed forces, he can veto legislation once, and he appoints ambassadors and some state officials.
